questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Who formulated the universal law of gravitation?
questions.explanation: Isaac Newton formulated the universal law of gravitation, published in Principia (1687). Earlier observations of falling bodies and planetary motion contributed to its development.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the universal law of gravitation state?

options.A: Every object falls at the same rate regardless of mass
options.B: Any two masses attract each other with a force proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centres
options.C: The force between two charges is inversely proportional to the square of the distance

questions.explanation: The universal law of gravitation states that any two masses attract each other; the force is proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centres.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Who formulated the three classical laws of motion?
questions.explanation: Isaac Newton formulated the three classical laws of motion in Principia (1687).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Newton's first law of motion state?

options.A: Net force equals the rate of change of momentum
options.B: A body remains at rest or in uniform straight-line motion unless acted upon by a net external force
options.C: For every action force there is an equal and opposite reaction force
options.D: Force is proportional to the product of masses

questions.explanation: Newton's first law, also known as the law of inertia, states that a body remains at rest or in uniform straight-line motion unless acted upon by a net external force.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Newton's second law of motion state?

options.A: A body remains at rest unless acted upon by a force
options.B: Net force equals the rate of change of momentum; for constant mass, F = ma
options.C: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction
options.D: Every mass attracts every other mass

questions.explanation: Newton's second law states that net force equals the rate of change of momentum; for constant mass, F = ma.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Newton's third law of motion state?

options.A: A body remains at rest unless acted upon by a net external force
options.B: Net force equals the rate of change of momentum
options.C: For every action force there is an equal and opposite reaction force acting on another body
options.D: Force is directly proportional to acceleration

questions.explanation: Newton's third law states that for every action force there is an equal and opposite reaction force acting on another body.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Who discovered electromagnetic induction?
questions.explanation: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831; Joseph Henry independently investigated related induction phenomena.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: In which year did Michael Faraday discover electromagnetic induction?
questions.explanation: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831. Joseph Henry independently investigated related induction phenomena.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is electromagnetic induction?

options.A: Production of an electromotive force when magnetic flux through a circuit changes
options.B: Production of heat when current flows through a resistor
options.C: Deflection of a magnetic needle near a current-carrying wire
options.D: Generation of a magnetic field by a permanent magnet

questions.explanation: Electromagnetic induction is the production of an electromotive force when magnetic flux through a circuit changes.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a practical application of electromagnetic induction?
questions.explanation: Practical applications of electromagnetic induction include electric generators, transformers, induction motors, induction heating and wireless charging.

options.A: Proportional to the product of masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centres
options.B: Proportional to the distance between masses
options.C: Inversely proportional to the product of masses

questions.explanation: The force is proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centres.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the relationship between force, mass and acceleration in Newton's second law for constant mass?
questions.explanation: For constant mass, Newton's second law is expressed as F = ma.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a use of X-rays?
questions.explanation: X-rays are used for medical imaging, CT scanning, security screening, materials analysis and crystallography; they are not used for generating electricity.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which particle determines an element's atomic number?
questions.explanation: The number of protons determines an element's atomic number.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What do free neutrons contribute to in research and reactors?

options.A: They are useful in research and reactors
options.C: They are only found in stars
options.D: They cannot be produced on Earth

questions.explanation: Neutrons contribute to nuclear mass, isotopes and nuclear stability; free neutrons are useful in research and reactors.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What did Rutherford's gold-foil experiment reveal about the volume of the atom?

options.A: Much of its volume is empty space
options.B: The entire volume is filled with positive charge
options.C: The nucleus occupies most of the volume

questions.explanation: Rutherford's gold-foil experiment showed that the atom contains a small, dense, positively charged nucleus, with much of its volume being empty space.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the germ theory?

options.A: Diseases are caused by bad air
options.B: Many infectious diseases are caused by specific microorganisms
options.C: Pasteur and Koch contributed major evidence
options.D: Semmelweis and Lister contributed preventive practices

questions.explanation: Germ theory states that many infectious diseases are caused by specific microorganisms, not by bad air. Pasteur and Koch were central; Semmelweis and Lister contributed preventive practices.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which scientist is known for polyphase motors and high-voltage electrical technology?
questions.explanation: Nikola Tesla is best known for alternating-current power systems, polyphase motors and high-voltage electrical technology.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which scientist's telescopic observations supported heliocentrism?
questions.explanation: Galileo Galilei is best known for telescopic astronomy, studies of motion and falling bodies, and observations supporting heliocentrism.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which Indian scientist is associated with radio/microwave research?
questions.explanation: Jagadish Chandra Bose is best known for pioneering work on radio/microwave research and plant physiological responses; he developed sensitive instruments.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which Indian scientist is associated with sugarcane research?
questions.explanation: Janaki Ammal is an Indian botanist and cytogeneticist known for plant breeding, sugarcane research and plant chromosome studies.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What was the significance of India's Chandrayaan-3 landing in 2023?

options.A: India achieved a controlled soft landing on the Moon with the Vikram lander, deploying the Pragyan rover near the lunar south-polar region
options.B: India landed humans on the Moon

questions.explanation: On 23 August 2023, India achieved a controlled soft landing on the Moon with the Vikram lander, deploying the Pragyan rover near the lunar south-polar region.
